projects.issues_checked: longest per-person age spread 14,237 d (39 y) against a 30 d collection-date spread; 383 samples / 218 persons, age and date both route R1
projects.cause: The ENA BioSample attribute 'host age' is present on only 36 of 383 samples and is misaligned with the rows it sits on. Subject 17 (titles 17_24052020, 17_03062020, 17_20062020; all male, host height 165 cm, BMI 22) carries 31, 61 and 70 years within 27 days, and 12 of the 17 subject ids with more than one aged sample carry conflicting ages. The misalignment is positional, not per-person: consecutive aliases deep_83, deep_85, deep_87, deep_90 all read 70 years across four different subject ids, and deep_91, deep_92, deep_93, deep_96, deep_98 all read 67 years. 'host subject id' itself is sound - across all 218 subject ids 'host sex', 'host height' and 'host body-mass index' are each single-valued, so the person grouping is not the defect. Individual values are inside the paper's patient age range (17-96), so no single value can be repaired from the archive.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJEB91718 do not derive age_at_collection_days from BioSample attribute 'host age'; clear age on all samples of this study. Keep 'host subject id' as the person key (do not ungroup).
projects.affected_samples: age: the 36 samples carrying 'host age' (aliases deep_3 through deep_98, e.g. SAMEA118689655, SAMEA118689662, SAMEA118689668); person grouping: unaffected, all 383 samples keep their subject id
projects.evidence_quote: The mean ± standard error of the mean age in years was 61.2 ± 1.3 (range, 17–96) for patients.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC11219902 (Front Microbiol 2024, Results), the study's own publication; cross-checked against ENA BioSamples SAMEA118689655 / SAMEA118689662 / SAMEA118689668
projects.note: Catalog age values 11312.8 / 22280.2 / 25550.0 days for subject 17 are 31 / 61 / 70 years x 365.25, confirming route R1 read 'host age' directly.

projects.issues_checked: longest per-person age spread 13,857 d (38 y) against a 31 d collection-date spread; 143 samples / 109 persons
projects.cause: Person grouping is sound: aliases are lt-<patient>-<sample number> and titles are 'Liver Transplant Patient N', and 105 of the 107 patients have a single host_age across their samples. Two patients carry contradictory per-record values: lt-054-01 (SAMN32942486) reads host_age 35 and lt-054-02 (SAMN32942487) reads host_age 73 thirteen days apart, both host_sex male; lt-105-01/02/03 (SAMN32942552/3/4) read host_age 58, 2 and 53 with host_sex female, female and male. These are per-record data-entry errors in host_age (and host_sex for patient 105), not a shared or reused subject id.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA928758 keep the lt-### patient number as the person key; clear age (and host_sex) for the samples of patients 054 and 105 only: SAMN32942486, SAMN32942487, SAMN32942552, SAMN32942553, SAMN32942554. Leave host_age on the other 138 samples.
projects.affected_samples: 5 samples: SAMN32942486, SAMN32942487 (patient 054); SAMN32942552, SAMN32942553, SAMN32942554 (patient 105)
projects.evidence_source: NCBI BioSample SAMN32942552 / SAMN32942553 / SAMN32942554 TITLE field (aliases lt-105-01/02/03), whose host_age attributes read 58, 2 and 53 and host_sex female, female and male
projects.note: No linked publication found: Europe PMC searches on PRJNA928758 and SRP419436 returned 0 hits, so the correct ages cannot be recovered from a paper or supplement.

projects.issues_checked: per-person collection-date spread 12,321 d (33.7 y) over 2 persons, and 15 samples dated before 1990
projects.cause: This is a genuine multi-decade longitudinal series, not a metadata defect. The study followed two healthy blood donors for more than 30 years; the 107 BioSamples are titled 'Subject1, TP1' ... and carry the attribute 'Subject' = 'Subject #1' (55 samples) or 'Subject #2' (52 samples), with collection_date running 1985-11-15 to 2019-08-10 at roughly 6-month intervals. The pre-1990 dates are real archived-plasma collection dates, not birth dates or defaults.
projects.correction_rule: Make no change to PRJNA785545: keep collection_date for all 107 samples and keep 'Subject' as the person key. Add PRJNA785545 to the allow-list for the >20-year follow-up and pre-1990 plausibility checks.
projects.affected_samples: none (all 107 samples correct; 15 of them dated 1985-1989)
projects.evidence_quote: We investigated the dynamics of blood anellomes in two healthy people followed up for more than 30 years.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC9175625 (Microbiol Spectr 2022), the study's own publication (abstract)
projects.note: Specimens are blood/plasma, not stool - worth checking that this study belongs in a gut-metagenome catalog.

projects.issues_checked: longest per-person age spread 11,688 d (32 y) against a 309 d date spread; 2 samples with age -365.2 d; 3,824 samples / 1,532 persons (iMSMS, Qiita study 11326)
projects.cause: Three separate defects, all small and all identifiable. (1) Negative ages are a missing-value sentinel: nine samples carry host_age -1, -2 or -957 with host_age_units 'Years'. (2) Six samples carry collection_timestamp '1905-07-08', which is the Excel 1900-system serial number 2016 rendered as a date; each is the '.B' re-sequencing replicate of a sample whose non-replicate twin carries collection_timestamp '2016' with the identical tube_id and host_age (e.g. SAMEA5858657 '11326.Q1.71802.0007.N.A.B' vs SAMEA5661729 '11326.Q1.71802.0007.N.A'), so the year 2016 is recoverable. (3) Exactly one of 3,548 titled samples has a host_subject_id that contradicts its own title and tube id: SAMEA5661854 is titled '11326.Q2.71601.0001.6.27.16' but carries host_subject_id 71602-0001. iMSMS pairs each MS case with a household control, and 71601-0001 and 71602-0001 are the two members of household H.0096, so this single record merges two different people into one person key and is the source of the 32-year age span.
projects.correction_rule: For PRJEB32762 apply three rules: (a) treat host_age <= 0 as missing and clear age for SAMEA10314058, SAMEA10314059, SAMEA10314138, SAMEA10314139, SAMEA10314761, SAMEA10314762, SAMEA10314783, SAMEA10314784, SAMEA10314785; (b) set collection_date to 2016 (year only) for SAMEA5858646, SAMEA5858657, SAMEA5858663, SAMEA5858664, SAMEA5858820, SAMEA5858846, whose collection_timestamp is the Excel serial 1905-07-08; (c) derive person_key from the five-digit + four-digit block of the sample title / tube_id rather than from host_subject_id, which fixes SAMEA5661854 to 71601-0001. Do not ungroup on 'household' - it is a separate, correct field.
projects.affected_samples: 9 samples for the negative-age rule, 6 for the 1905-07-08 date rule, 1 (SAMEA5661854) for the person key; the remaining ~3,808 samples are unaffected
projects.evidence_source: ENA BioSample SAMEA5661854 TITLE element, whose host_subject_id attribute on the same record reads 71602-0001 and whose household attribute reads H.0096
projects.note: Excel 1900-system serial 2016 renders as 1905-07-08, verified arithmetically; the twin records carrying literal '2016' confirm it independently. host_age is 'N/A' in the current ENA records for all samples of 71602-0001, so the catalog's 8035.5 / 19723.5 day values came from an earlier snapshot or the supplementary route.

projects.issues_checked: per-person collection-date spread 7,344 d (20.1 y) over 7 persons in a 2022 crossover trial
projects.cause: A two-digit year typo, not a real 20-year gap. Every participant has four visits V3-V6 at 2-4 week spacing, and the whole study runs 2022-04-13 to 2022-07-26. Two records read 2002 instead of 2022: SAMN37947821 (alias VP08V4, 'VP08: post-placebo') reads 2002-05-19 between VP08V3 2022-05-05 and VP08V5 2022-06-13, and SAMN37947814 (alias VP06V5, 'VP06: pre-test') reads 2002-06-13 between VP06V4 2022-05-23 and VP06V6 2022-06-27. Both fall exactly where the visit sequence requires when the year is read as 2022.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA1031616 set collection_date 2002-05-19 -> 2022-05-19 for SAMN37947821 and 2002-06-13 -> 2022-06-13 for SAMN37947814. No other sample needs a change and no person needs ungrouping.
projects.affected_samples: 2 samples: SAMN37947821 (VP08V4) and SAMN37947814 (VP06V5). Only the first was in the flagged input; the second was found by scanning all 28 samples.
projects.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics sequencing data pre- and post- Veillonella and/or Placebo supplementation in a randomized controlled crossover pilot study
projects.evidence_source: ENA study PRJNA1031616 study_description (ENA portal API), with ENA BioSamples SAMN37947814 and SAMN37947821 and the 26 sibling samples dated 2022-04-13 to 2022-07-26

projects.issues_checked: one sample with age 43,464.8 d (119.0 y), route R1
projects.cause: SAMN10886036 (alias stool_037) carries BioSample attribute age = 119 while the other 155 samples of the study run from -959 to 71 with a median of 48. The cohort is 77 adult women with fibromyalgia and 79 controls, so 119 years is not attainable; the same attribute also carries an obvious sentinel (-959 on SAMN10886139, alias stool_140), which shows the column is not validated. collection_date is the literal string 'missing' on all 156 samples and host is 'missing', so there is no internal cross-check, and no per-sample age table is published for this project, so the true value is not recoverable. 119 is most consistent with a transcription error in a two-digit age rather than a unit or birth-year misread.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA521587 treat BioSample 'age' values outside 18-100 as missing: clear age for SAMN10886036 (age 119) and SAMN10886139 (age -959). Keep age for the other 154 samples.
projects.affected_samples: 2 samples: SAMN10886036 (age 119, in the flagged input) and SAMN10886139 (age -959, found while scanning all 156 samples)
projects.evidence_quote: The microbiomes of 77 women with FM and that of 79 control participants were compared using 16S rRNA gene amplification and whole-genome sequencing.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMID 31219947 (Pain 2019, abstract), the study's own publication; ENA BioSamples SAMN10886036 and SAMN10886139
projects.note: Provisional on the corrected value: the record and the paper establish that 119 is impossible but neither gives the right age, so clearing is the only safe action.

projects.issues_checked: one sample with age 40,543 d (111.0 y), route R2 (supplementary table)
projects.cause: This is a longevity cohort and 111 years is the documented cohort maximum, not an error. The ENA study record describes 151 healthy people from Yongfu County, Guangxi, China, including 29 centenarians aged 100-111. 40,543 days is exactly 111.0 x 365.25, i.e. the supplementary-table value for SAMN11960414 (alias S5012) read correctly. The BioSample record itself carries no age attribute, which is why the catalog used route R2.
projects.correction_rule: Make no change to PRJNA542578; keep age for SAMN11960414 and allow ages up to 111 years in this study (do not apply a generic >110 y cut here).
projects.evidence_quote: 29 individuals aged 100-111 (Centenarians) and 46 individuals aged 90-100(Nonagenarians) and 40 individuals aged 60-90(Elderly) and 36 individuals aged 20-60(Middle-aged)
projects.evidence_source: ENA study PRJNA542578 study_description (ENA portal API)

projects.issues_checked: four samples with ages 40,448-43,830 d (110.7-120.0 y), route R1
projects.cause: The BioSample attribute 'age' in this project is a submission row counter, not an age. Across the 178 samples it takes 178 distinct integers spanning 1 to 180 (only 58 and 60 are absent), each used exactly once, assigned in the order of the submitted sample list: SN8_RNA_WK8 = 1, SN8_RNA_WK4 = 2, SN8_RNA_WK2 = 3, SN8_RNA_VISIT-1 = 4, and so on. Within a participant it increments across timepoints, which no age in years does on a 2-8 week trial schedule. The trial itself enrolled 15 adults with a median age of 33 years, so values of 111-120 cannot be ages. The flagged values are exactly 111, 112, 114 and 120 multiplied by 365.25.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA1138254 do not use BioSample attribute 'age' for age_at_collection_days; it is a 1..180 record serial number. Clear age for all 178 samples of the study.
projects.affected_samples: all 178 samples (the 4 flagged ones - SAMN42687897, SAMN42687898, SAMN42687900, SAMN42687906 - are only the tail of the counter)
projects.evidence_quote: In all, 15 patients participated in the study (median age 33 years, 11 attributed male sex at birth).
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC11831226 (2025), the PSC-Vanc trial publication (Results); ENA/NCBI BioSample 'age' attribute for all 178 samples of PRJNA1138254

projects.cause: The patient arm's 'collection date' is a date of birth. All 20 samples whose sample description is 'patient' (aliases U18-U40) carry dates from 1942-10-24 to 1998-11-06, while all 21 samples described as 'control' (aliases C18-C195) carry 2016-02-12 to 2021-08-31; the cohort was recruited in Bern from 2016 to 2021, so a 1942 stool metagenome is impossible. Treating the patient dates as birth dates and computing age at 2021 gives a mean of 44.5 years, which matches the paper's patient mean age exactly (M = 44.5, SD = 16.3), and the records' own 'age' attribute for the same 20 samples has mean 44.5 / SD 16.7. The two columns are not paired row-by-row (U28, dated 1942, carries age 40; U26, dated 1998, carries age 78), so only the multiset agrees - the dates are birth dates that were sorted independently of the ages.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJEB55787 clear collection_date for the 20 samples whose BioSample description is 'patient' (aliases U18-U40, including SAMEA120325594, SAMEA120325595, SAMEA120325599, SAMEA120325602); these are dates of birth. Keep collection_date for the 21 'control' samples. Set the study-level sampling period to 2016-2021 from the paper. Keep the 'age' attribute as the age source.
projects.affected_samples: the 20 'patient' samples (4 of them were flagged as pre-1990; the other 16 carry 1990-1998 birth dates that the pre-1990 filter missed)
projects.evidence_quote: They were recruited from either the ward or the retina outpatient clinic in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University Hospital Bern (Inselspital), located in Switzerland from 2016 until 2021.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC11077820 (2024), the study's own publication (Methods and Table 1); ENA BioSamples SAMEA120325584-SAMEA120325624
projects.note: Because age and birth date are not row-matched, the per-sample birth date cannot be used to recompute age either; the 'age' attribute should be kept as-is.

projects.cause: These are genuinely 1980s specimens. The study sequenced archived stool from an NCI colorectal-cancer case-control study recruited in Washington DC in 1985-1987; the stools were freeze-dried and held at -40 C until shotgun sequencing around 2015. '1985/1987' is a correct ISO-style interval covering the recruitment window, not a placeholder or a birth year.
projects.correction_rule: Keep the collection date for all 110 PRJEB12449 samples, but record it as the interval 1985-1987 rather than collapsing it to collection_year = 1985; the per-sample date within that window is not recorded anywhere. Add PRJEB12449 to the allow-list for the pre-1990 plausibility check.
projects.affected_samples: all 110 samples carry the same interval; none needs a value change, only the year-flattening should be revisited
projects.evidence_quote: Briefly, CRC cases and frequency matched controls who were waiting surgery for non-oncological and non-gastrointestinal conditions were recruited from 1985 to 1987 in Washington DC, United States.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC4865240 (PLoS One 2016), the study's own publication (Materials and Methods, Primary study population)

projects.cause: These are archived Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) specimens from the enrolment visits of 1984-1985, sequenced in 2023 (the sample aliases end in '202311'). The paper states the cohort was enrolled in MACS between 1984 and 1985 and that the profiled gut and oral specimens are from the first clinic visit, before HIV-1 infection. '1984/1985' is a correct interval, not a default or a birth year.
projects.correction_rule: Keep the collection date for all 463 PRJNA1303200 samples but record it as the interval 1984-1985 rather than collection_year = 1984; the per-visit date is not in the archive record. Add PRJNA1303200 to the allow-list for the pre-1990 plausibility check.
projects.affected_samples: all 463 samples (235 gut, 228 oral) carry the same interval; none needs a value change
projects.evidence_quote: This study includes 239 MSM enrolled in the MACS between 1984 and 1985.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC12635353 (2025), the study's own publication (Results)

projects.cause: These are real archival serum collection dates. The study is two registry-linked nested case-control studies in which banked Swedish serum drawn years before a multiple sclerosis diagnosis was sequenced, so dates decades before the 2018 deposit are expected. The dates are internally consistent: they form a smooth distribution from 1976 to 2007 rather than clustering on one value, and in all 50 matched case/control pairs where both members carry a real year the two years are identical, which is what date-matched control selection produces. The pre-1990 values are therefore not birth years, freezer dates or defaults.
projects.correction_rule: Keep the pre-1990 collection_date values for PRJNA471187 and add the study to the allow-list for the pre-1990 check. Separately, treat collection_date '1905' (71 samples) and 'not applicable' (6 samples) in this project as missing rather than as real years.
projects.affected_samples: the 64 flagged samples are correct; a different set of 77 samples in the same project (71 with '1905', 6 with 'not applicable') carries sentinel values and should be cleared
projects.evidence_quote: Serum samples taken before diagnosis as well as samples from matched control subjects were selected.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMID 29772404 (Virology 2018, abstract), the study's own publication; ENA BioSample collection_date values for all 342 samples of PRJNA471187

projects.cause: A single placeholder applied to the whole deposit. Every one of the 127 BioSamples carries exactly 1980-06-01, including the five serial recipient samples per recipient (timepoint attribute 'Timepoint 00' through 'Timepoint 04') that were by design drawn weeks to months apart after transfusion, plus the donor samples ('Donor 01' ... 'Donor 07') drawn before it. One identical date for all of them cannot be the true collection date. The value is the closing month of the source cohort's enrolment window: the NHLBI Transfusion-Transmitted Viruses Study ran from July 1974 through June 1980. The true per-sample dates are not in the archive record and are not given in the publication, so they cannot be recovered.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA679286 clear collection_date for all 127 samples (uniform placeholder 1980-06-01) and record the sampling window 1974-07 to 1980-06 at study level only. Keep the person grouping: host_subject_id is R## for the recipients' own timepoints and R##D## for their donors, which is already correct.
projects.evidence_quote: To characterize the changes in serum virome compositions of transfusion recipients, we studied pretransfusion and posttransfusion serum samples from subjects enrolled in the Transfusion-Transmitted Viruses Study (TTVS) from July 1974 through June 1980.
projects.evidence_source: Europe PMC PMC4600124 (J Virol 2015, Results) describing the same TTVS specimen set; ENA study PRJNA679286 study_description names the NHLBI Transfusion-transmitted Viruses Study

projects.cause: '1989/2018' is the biobank's whole collection interval, carried unchanged onto every sample, not a per-sample collection date. The study drew 476 archived diagnostic serum samples collected between 1989 and 2018 from Uppsala Biobank and sequenced them as 23 pools grouped by diagnosis and age, so the 48 deposited records each cover several donors and several collection years and no single date exists for them. Collapsing the interval to collection_year = 1989 is what produced the pre-1990 flag.
projects.correction_rule: In PRJNA1036630 clear collection_date and collection_year for all 48 samples; keep 1989-2018 as a study-level sampling window only. Do not record collection_year = 1989 for any sample.
projects.evidence_quote: A total of 476 patient samples, collected between 1989 and 2018, representing different diagnoses and ages, were analyzed.
projects.evidence_source: ENA study PRJNA1036630 study_description (ENA portal API)
projects.note: Specimens are pooled pediatric serum, not stool; the pooling is a second reason no per-sample date exists.

projects.cause: The flagged record is not a human sample and nothing contradicts its date. SAMN29756906 is titled 'tick metagenome' with alias and sample ID DALBE3, host 'not applicable', geographic location USA: Minnesota, and collection_date 1989 - an archived arthropod specimen in a Francisella bait-capture methods study whose other 57 samples are air filters (43), lymph aspirates (9), dust (3) and two further ticks dated 2010-04-17 and 2011-05-29. A 1989 collection date for a curated tick specimen is ordinary and the archive gives no conflicting value, so there is nothing to correct in the date itself.
projects.correction_rule: Keep collection_date 1989 for SAMN29756906 and add it to the allow-list for the pre-1990 check. Separately, flag PRJNA857715 for scope review: it contains no human gut samples (air filter, dust, lymph aspirate and tick metagenomes only). Also treat collection_date '1905-07-08' on SAMN29756860 (lymph aspirate F1069) as missing - it is an Excel 1900-system serial number, not a 1905 date.
projects.affected_samples: 1 flagged sample (SAMN29756906) is correct; SAMN29756860 in the same project carries a separate bad date
projects.evidence_quote: Data from air samples enriched with a Francisella bait system
projects.evidence_source: ENA study PRJNA857715 study_description (ENA portal API); NCBI BioSample SAMN29756906 (title 'tick metagenome', host 'not applicable', collection_date 1989)
projects.note: Provisional: the date is accepted because nothing contradicts it, not because a source states it. The substantive issue here is scope, not plausibility - no human gut specimen exists in this project.

declared_limitations: No publication could be located for PRJNA928758 (Europe PMC on PRJNA928758 and SRP419436 both returned 0 hits), so its age determination rests on the BioSample records alone and the correct ages are unrecoverable.

PRJNA521587's corrected age is unrecoverable: the Minerbi 2019 paper is not open access in Europe PMC and no per-sample age table was found, so only the 'impossible value' call is firm (flagged provisional).
PRJNA857715's 'keep' rests on absence of a contradicting source rather than a positive statement of the 1989 tick collection date (flagged provisional, confidence 0.7).
